หลักฐานทางการของเทศบาลเมืองตะกั่วป่าระบุ: Official evidence from Takua Pa Municipality identifies Bun Thao Kong A Shrine as the town's first shrine and places it in the old port district known as Chap Se or Chap Sao. This locates the shrine within Takua Pa's history of waterborne trade and old-market activity, but the documents found give neither a construction start year nor the name of an individual founder
ฐานข้อมูลชุมชนตลาดใหญ่ระบุว่าผู้สร้างเป็: The Talat Yai Community database identifies the builders as Chinese immigrants who came to Takua Pa to mine, mentioning groups such as Hokkien, Hainanese, and Cantonese. This presents the shrine as both a ritual site and an anchor for the workers and merchants of a mining town. However, there is not enough direct evidence to determine which group founded it or what specific role the shrine played in the port system
เทศบาลยังบันทึกว่าภายในมี “กระถางธูปที่ร: The municipality also records an incense burner “presented by King Rama VI”. This is evidence of a past relationship between the local shrine and the Siamese state, but the year, occasion, and provenance of the object are not specified

สิ่งที่ยืนยันได้คือในปี 2564 มีการบันทึก: What can be verified is that in 2021 (พ.ศ. 2564), a video recorded the Sae Yit ceremony for Phra Hok Tek Jiah Sin or Pae Kong at Pun Thao Kong Am Shrine in Chap Se, while another video mentions the oil-bathing ceremony, Phra La ceremony, and bringing in the sacred fire. This shows that the shrine was still a ritual space for Takua Pa descendants at that time
